ownership_summary: Listed on Bahrain Bourse since 1990 (trading code ABC). The Central Bank of Libya is the majority shareholder and ultimate parent with 59.37%, after buying ADIA's 17.72% stake in 2010. The Kuwait Investment Authority holds 29.69%, and others below 5% hold 10.94% (AR 2025).

shareholders.holder: Other shareholders with less than 5% each (incl. free float)

government_link: Yes - controlled by the Central Bank of Libya (59.37%), with the Kuwait Investment Authority holding 29.69% (AR 2025, S5 p.106).
group_structure: Arab Banking Corporation (B.S.C.) is the listed Bahraini parent and runs wholesale banking from Manama with branches in New York, DIFC (Dubai) and Singapore, plus a rep office in Tripoli. Principal subsidiaries at 31 Dec 2025 (S4 note 21): ABC International Bank plc (UK, 100%), ABC SA (France, 100%), ABC Islamic Bank (E.C.) (Bahrain, 100%), Bank ABC Jordan (87.0%), Banco ABC Brasil S.A. (63.5%), ABC Algeria (88.9%), Bank ABC Egypt (99.6%), ABC Tunisie (100%) and Arab Financial Services B.S.C. (c) (AFS, cards and fintech, 98.0%). ila Bank is Bank ABC's digital mobile-only bank. In Bahrain it is a retail branch of the parent ('ila Bank - Retail Branch'), and the H1 2026 statements describe it as a banking space within retail consumer banking. A 2025 project to carve it out as a separate subsidiary is under way (S5). ila also runs in Jordan through Bank ABC Jordan. None of these units has its own file, so all are recorded here.

footprint: Presence in 15 countries covering 25+ markets (S9). GCC: Bahrain (HQ, Bank ABC Islamic, ila Bank, AFS) and UAE (DIFC branch). Elsewhere: Jordan, Egypt, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya (rep office), UK, France, Germany, Italy, Türkiye, USA, Brazil and Singapore. AR 2025 retail branch counts: Cairo 52, Algiers 24, Amman 19, Tunis 17. In the GCC, retail is offered only through ila in Bahrain (S5 p.10, S3 note 1).
customer_segments: Corporates, financial institutions and sovereign entities (wholesale, Islamic wholesale, trade and transaction banking). Middle-market corporates in Brazil. Retail and SME customers in Jordan, Egypt, Algeria and Tunisia. Digital mass and mass-affluent retail through ila (Bahrain, Jordan), including the ila Premium tier and Gulf Air card targeting the affluent segment (S5, S16).
business_lines: Operating segments (S3 note 9): MENA subsidiaries (retail, corporate and treasury in North Africa and Levant); International wholesale banking (corporate and structured finance, trade finance, Islamic banking, syndications); Group treasury (Bahrain HO, New York, London); ABC Brasil; Others (Head Office, AFS and ila Bank). Group Treasury & Financial Markets includes Capital Markets, Financial Markets, Asset Management & Custody and Corporate Treasury (S5 p.17). Self-described as offering 'a leading universal banking proposition' (S5 p.9). Type set to Wholesale bank because of the CBB licence and the revenue mix.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Bank ABC is a wholesale-led group (CBB conventional wholesale licence) with no private banking or wealth management franchise found in the GCC. Asset Management & Custody sits within Group Treasury & Financial Markets (Head of Asset Management Karim El Sherif). Funds under management held in a fiduciary capacity were USD 24.4bn at end-2025, with no split by entity (S4, S5, S8). In the GCC, retail investing runs only through ila Bank (Bahrain), the group's mobile-only bank (launched 2019). Its in-app 'Investments' tab offers Bahrain Government Securities (T-bills, development bonds and sukuk, connected directly to the CBB, launched Sep 2024, now from a BHD 1,000 bid, no custody fee) and digital Gold & Silver Investment Accounts (from 0.010oz gold / 1oz silver, with a suitability questionnaire). It also offers fixed deposits and Shari'a-compliant alburaq Wakala investments (S13-S15, S17). ila is moving upmarket through ila Premium and the 2025 Gulf Air co-branded card ('expanding its presence in the affluent segment'), and is being carved out as a standalone digital bank (S5, S16). No funds, equities, model portfolios or advisory were found in ila.

digital_investing.detail: ila Bank app (Bahrain) 'Investments' tab: (1) Bahrain Government Securities (T-bills 3/6/12 months, bonds, Islamic sukuk) bought directly in-app through a direct CBB connection, launched 8 Sep 2024 with a BHD 10,000 minimum, now 'minimum BHD 1,000 bid', no custody fee; (2) Gold & Silver Investment Accounts with live prices and portfolio tracking (unallocated, no physical delivery), launch date not found (AR 2025 mentions a 2025 rollout of precious-metals capabilities in Financial Markets). Also fixed deposits, alburaq Wakala, Al Kanz prize-linked savings and Jamiyah (S13-S15, S17, S21, S5 p.52).

opportunities: ila's in-app 'Investments' tab offers only government securities and gold/silver; no funds, equities, model portfolios or advisory were found (S13, S14, S21).

ila is pushing into the affluent segment (Gulf Air co-brand, ila Premium) and is being carved out as a standalone digital bank 'ready for further expansion' with a 'regional growth strategy' (S5 pp.30, 45, 57).
The group reuses ila's technology across MENA retail (Egypt Blue App 2025; Algeria and Tunisia planned 2026), so a product added to ila could be reused across five retail markets (S5 p.53).
A new Group CEO took office in Aug 2026 after a period of acting leadership; strategy may be reset (S7).
barriers: Wholesale-led group with no private banking or wealth franchise found; GCC retail is limited to ila in Bahrain (S3 note 1, S5).
Several C-suite roles are acting (CFO, Wholesale, Credit & Risk), and H1 2026 attributable profit fell 27% on conflict-related provisions (S1, S6).
ila runs on Temenos core banking, so integrations must fit that stack (S5).
The ila alburaq customer base needs Shari'a-compliant products (S17).
